KeyStory: Shinab's city shared Sodom's defeat in the Valley of Siddim, where the kings fell into tar pits.
LifeLesson: Empires rise and fall, but God's promise to Abram outlasted every king of his day.

Name: Shobal
Summary: Shobal was a son of Seir the Horite, and the father of Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
KeyStory: Shobal is named among Seir's sons and among the dukes of the Horites.
RelatedPeople: Seir; Alvan; Manahath; Ebal; Shepho; Onam
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Shuah, Son of Keturah
Summary: Shuah was a son of Abraham and Keturah, named among the six children of Abraham's later marriage.
KeyStory: Shuah appears in the genealogy of Abraham's later children, who were sent eastward with gifts.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Shuah the Canaanite
Summary: Shuah was a Canaanite whose daughter married Judah, and whose grandsons were Er, Onan, and Shelah.
KeyStory: Judah married Shuah's daughter in Canaan, and her sons' story became part of the line leading to David.
RelatedPeople: Judah; Er; Onan; Shelah, Son of Judah
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Shuni
Summary: Shuni was a son of Gad, named among the children of Israel who went down into Egypt.
KeyStory: Shuni appears in the list of Jacob's family that came into Egypt.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Sidon
Summary: Sidon was the son of Canaan, named among the nations that spread across the earth after the flood.
KeyStory: Sidon appears in the Table of Nations, tracing the peoples of the earth back to Noah's family.
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Simeon, Son of Jacob
Summary: Simeon was the second son of Jacob by Leah, and the father of Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul.
KeyStory: Simeon joined Levi in avenging Dinah at Shechem, and his tribe later scattered within Israel, just as Jacob had foretold.
RelatedPeople: Jacob; Leah; Levi; Dinah; Jemuel; Jamin; Ohad; Jachin; Zohar, Son of Simeon; Shaul
LifeLesson: Anger acted on without God leaves a legacy of scattering — Simeon's story is a warning.

Name: Tarshish
Summary: Tarshish was the son of Javan, named among the nations that spread across the earth after the flood.
KeyStory: Tarshish appears in the Table of Nations, tracing the peoples of the earth back to Noah's family.
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Tebah
Summary: Tebah was a son of Nahor by his concubine Reumah.
KeyStory: Tebah is named among Reumah's four sons in the record of Nahor's family.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Tema
Summary: Tema was a son of Ishmael, named among the children born after Abraham's first family.
KeyStory: Tema appears in the genealogy of Abraham's later children and their descendants.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Teman
Summary: Teman was a son of Eliphaz, named among the dukes of Edom.
KeyStory: Teman appears in the record of Edom's dukes, the chiefs descended from Esau.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Terah
Summary: Terah was the son of Nahor and the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran. He lived 205 years.
KeyStory: Terah led his family out of Ur toward Canaan, but they settled in Haran, where he died — and Abram's journey continued from there.
RelatedPeople: Nahor, Father of Terah; Abraham; Nahor, Brother of Abraham; Haran; Lot
LifeLesson: A journey can stall with one generation and resume with the next; God is patient with families.

Name: Thahash
Summary: Thahash was a son of Nahor by his concubine Reumah.
KeyStory: Thahash is named among Reumah's four sons in the record of Nahor's family.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Tidal
Summary: Tidal was the king of Goiim, called 'king of nations,' who joined Chedorlaomer's alliance.
KeyStory: Tidal marched with the eastern kings against the cities of the plain and was driven back by Abram.
LifeLesson: Empires rise and fall, but God's promise to Abram outlasted every king of his day.

Name: Timna
Role: Sister of Lotan; Concubine of Eliphaz
Summary: Timna was the sister of Lotan, daughter of Seir, and the concubine of Eliphaz, to whom she bore Amalek.
KeyStory: Timna links two houses of Edom: Seir's Horite family by birth, and Esau's line by her son Amalek.
RelatedPeople: Lotan; Seir; Eliphaz, Son of Esau; Amalek
LifeLesson: God names women in genealogies where the world might forget them.

Name: Timnah
Summary: Timnah was a duke of Edom, named among the chiefs who ruled by their families and dwelling places.
KeyStory: Timnah appears in the closing list of Edom's dukes, the chiefs descended from Esau.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Tiras
Summary: Tiras was the son of Japheth, named among the nations that spread across the earth after the flood.
KeyStory: Tiras appears in the Table of Nations, tracing the peoples of the earth back to Noah's family.
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Togarmah
Summary: Togarmah was the son of Gomer, named among the nations that spread across the earth after the flood.
KeyStory: Togarmah appears in the Table of Nations, tracing the peoples of the earth back to Noah's family.
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Tola
Summary: Tola was a son of Issachar, named among the children of Israel who went down into Egypt.
KeyStory: Tola appears in the list of Jacob's family that came into Egypt.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Tubal-cain
Summary: Tubal-cain was the son of Lamech and Zillah, an instructor of everyone who works in bronze and iron.
KeyStory: Tubal-cain forged tools and weapons from metal, opening the age of craftsmanship.
RelatedPeople: Lamech, Son of Methusael; Zillah; Naamah
LifeLesson: Skill and craftsmanship are God-given — and like every gift, they can serve good or harm.

Name: Tubal
Summary: Tubal was the son of Japheth, named among the nations that spread across the earth after the flood.
KeyStory: Tubal appears in the Table of Nations, tracing the peoples of the earth back to Noah's family.
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Uz, Son of Aram
Summary: Uz was a son of Aram and a grandson of Shem, named in the Table of Nations.
KeyStory: Uz appears among Aram's sons, one of the branches of Shem's line after the flood.
RelatedPeople: Aram, Son of Shem; Hul; Gether; Mash
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Uz, Son of Dishan
Summary: Uz was a son of Dishan and a grandson of Seir the Horite.
KeyStory: Uz is named with his brother Aran among Dishan's children.
LifeLesson: Three men named Uz appear in Genesis, and God knows each one apart.

Name: Uz, Son of Nahor
Summary: Uz, also called Huz, was the firstborn son of Nahor and Milcah, and the brother of Buz.
KeyStory: Uz heads the list of the eight children Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham's brother.
RelatedPeople: Nahor, Brother of Abraham; Milcah; Buz
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Uzal
Summary: Uzal was the son of Joktan, named among the nations that spread across the earth after the flood.
KeyStory: Uzal appears in the Table of Nations, tracing the peoples of the earth back to Noah's family.
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Zaavan
Summary: Zaavan was a son of Ezer and a grandson of Seir the Horite.
KeyStory: Zaavan is named among Ezer's three children.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Zebulun
Summary: Zebulun was the tenth son of Jacob, the sixth by Leah, and the father of Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
KeyStory: Zebulun's tribe later dwelt by the seashore, just as Jacob had blessed him.
RelatedPeople: Jacob; Leah; Sered; Elon, Son of Zebulun; Jahleel
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Zepho
Summary: Zepho was a son of Eliphaz, named among the dukes of Edom.
KeyStory: Zepho appears in the record of Edom's dukes, the chiefs descended from Esau.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Zerah of Bozrah
Summary: Zerah of Bozrah was the father of Jobab, who reigned as king in Edom.
KeyStory: Zerah is named only as Jobab's father, in the list of Edom's kings — a different Zerah from Judah's and Reuel's sons.
LifeLesson: Three men named Zerah appear in Genesis, and God knows each one apart.

Name: Zerah, Son of Judah
Summary: Zerah was the twin son of Judah and Tamar, whose hand came out first at birth, marked with a scarlet thread.
KeyStory: Zerah's scarlet thread marked him first, but his brother Pharez was born before him and carried the line forward.
LifeLesson: Being first out of the gate is not the same as carrying the promise.

Name: Zerah, Son of Reuel
Summary: Zerah was a son of Reuel and a grandson of Esau by Bashemath, Ishmael's daughter, and one of the dukes of Edom.
KeyStory: Zerah is named among Reuel's four sons and among the dukes that came of Reuel in Edom.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Zibeon
Summary: Zibeon was a son of Seir the Horite, and the father of Ajah and Anah.
KeyStory: Zibeon is named among Seir's sons and among the dukes of the Horites.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Zillah
Summary: Zillah was Lamech's other wife and the mother of Tubal-cain and Naamah.
KeyStory: Zillah listened as Lamech boasted of his revenge, a dark moment in the early story of humanity.
RelatedPeople: Lamech, Son of Methusael; Tubal-cain; Naamah
LifeLesson: Even in a household marked by violence, God still knew Zillah by name.

Name: Zilpah
Summary: Zilpah was Leah's handmaid, given to Jacob as a wife, and the mother of Gad and Asher.
KeyStory: When Leah stopped bearing children, she gave Zilpah to Jacob, and Zilpah bore Gad and then Asher.
LifeLesson: God hears the unheard: Zilpah's sons became two tribes of Israel.

Name: Zimran
Summary: Zimran was a son of Abraham and Keturah, named among the children born after Abraham's first family.
KeyStory: Zimran appears in the genealogy of Abraham's later children and their descendants.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Ziphion
Summary: Ziphion was a son of Gad, named among the children of Israel who went down into Egypt.
KeyStory: Ziphion appears in the list of Jacob's family that came into Egypt.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Zohar, Father of Ephron
Summary: Zohar was the father of Ephron the Hittite, from whom Abraham bought the cave of Machpelah.
KeyStory: Zohar is named only as Ephron's father, in the transaction that gave Abraham his first owned land in Canaan.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Zohar, Son of Simeon
Summary: Zohar was a son of Simeon and a grandson of Jacob, named among the family that went into Egypt.
KeyStory: Zohar is named among Simeon's six sons — a different Zohar from the father of Ephron.
RelatedPeople: Simeon, Son of Jacob; Jemuel; Jamin; Ohad; Jachin; Shaul
LifeLesson: Two men can share a name and walk very different paths; God knows each one.

Name: Abiasaph, Son of Korah
Summary: Abiasaph was a son of Korah, the Levite, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Abiasaph is named with his brothers Assir and Elkanah among Korah's sons.
RelatedPeople: Korah, Son of Izhar; Assir, Son of Korah; Elkanah, Son of Korah
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Abihu
Summary: Abihu was a son of Aaron and Elisheba, and one of the priests of Israel.
KeyStory: Abihu went up Mount Sinai with Moses and saw God, but later offered strange fire with his brother Nadab and died.
LifeLesson: Closeness to God is no substitute for obedience: Abihu saw God and still offered strange fire.

Name: Ahisamach
Summary: Ahisamach was of the tribe of Dan, and the father of Aholiab, the craftsman of the tabernacle.
KeyStory: Ahisamach is named only as Aholiab's father, in the record of the tabernacle's builders.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Aholiab
Summary: Aholiab, also spelled Oholiab, was the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, and Bezaleel's fellow craftsman on the tabernacle.
KeyStory: God gave Aholiab skill alongside Bezaleel, and together they made the tabernacle, the ark, and the priestly garments.
LifeLesson: Art and craftsmanship are Spirit-given gifts, made for God's house.

Name: Amminadab
Summary: Amminadab was the father of Elisheba, Aaron's wife, and of Naashon, the prince of Judah.
KeyStory: Amminadab's children tied the priestly line to Judah's royal line: his daughter married Aaron, his son led Judah.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Amram
Role: Father of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
Summary: Amram was a son of Kohath, of the tribe of Levi, and the husband of Jochebed. His children were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.
KeyStory: Amram married Jochebed, and their son Moses, hidden at birth from Pharaoh's decree, became the deliverer of Israel.
LifeLesson: Faithful parents in dark times can raise the very person God will use.

Name: Assir, Son of Korah
Summary: Assir was a son of Korah, the Levite, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Assir is named with his brothers Elkanah and Abiasaph among Korah's sons.
RelatedPeople: Korah, Son of Izhar; Elkanah, Son of Korah; Abiasaph, Son of Korah
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Bezaleel
Summary: Bezaleel, also spelled Bezalel, was the son of Uri, of the tribe of Judah, and the chief craftsman of the tabernacle.
KeyStory: God filled Bezaleel with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, understanding, and knowledge, to design and build the tabernacle and all its furnishings.
LifeLesson: Art and craftsmanship are Spirit-given gifts, made for God's house.

Name: Eleazar
Summary: Eleazar was a son of Aaron and Elisheba, and the priest who succeeded Aaron after his death.
KeyStory: Eleazar served through the wilderness years, stood with Joshua at the division of the land, and carried the priesthood after Aaron.
RelatedPeople: Aaron; Elisheba; Nadab; Abihu; Ithamar; Phinehas
LifeLesson: Faithfulness over a long life is its own kind of greatness.

Name: Eliezer, Son of Moses
Summary: Eliezer was the second son of Moses and Zipporah, born in Midian — a different Eliezer from Abraham's steward.
KeyStory: Moses named him Eliezer, saying, 'The God of my father was my help, and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.'
LifeLesson: Two men can share a name and walk very different paths; God knows each one.

Name: Elisheba
Summary: Elisheba was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Naashon, and the wife of Aaron. She bore him Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
KeyStory: Elisheba became the mother of Israel's priestly line, standing at the head of the family that would serve in the tabernacle.
RelatedPeople: Aaron; Amminadab; Naashon; Nadab; Abihu; Eleazar; Ithamar
LifeLesson: God names women in genealogies where the world might forget them.

Name: Elkanah, Son of Korah
Summary: Elkanah was a son of Korah, the Levite, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe — a different Elkanah from Samuel's father.
KeyStory: Elkanah is named with his brothers Assir and Abiasaph among Korah's sons.
RelatedPeople: Korah, Son of Izhar; Assir, Son of Korah; Abiasaph, Son of Korah
LifeLesson: Two men can share a name and walk very different paths; God knows each one.

Name: Elzaphan
Summary: Elzaphan was a son of Uzziel and a grandson of Kohath, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Elzaphan and his brother Mishael were called by Moses to carry the bodies of Nadab and Abihu out of the camp.
LifeLesson: Obedience sometimes means hard, holy work no one else wants to do.

Name: Gershom
Summary: Gershom was the firstborn son of Moses and Zipporah, born in Midian during Moses' exile.
KeyStory: Moses named him Gershom, saying, 'I have been a stranger in a strange land.'
RelatedPeople: Moses; Zipporah; Eliezer, Son of Moses; Jethro
LifeLesson: Even in exile, God was building Moses' family for the journey ahead.

Name: Hebron, Son of Kohath
Summary: Hebron was a son of Kohath and a grandson of Levi, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Hebron is named among Kohath's four sons — Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel — in the record of Levi's house.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Hur
Summary: Hur was a companion of Moses who held up his hands during the battle with Amalek, and who was left in charge of the people with Aaron while Moses was on the mountain.
KeyStory: When Moses' hands grew heavy, Aaron and Hur held them up until sunset, and Israel prevailed over Amalek.
LifeLesson: Victory often comes through the friends who hold your arms up when you cannot.

Name: Ithamar
Summary: Ithamar was the youngest son of Aaron and Elisheba, and one of the priests of Israel.
KeyStory: Ithamar oversaw the Levites' work on the tabernacle, keeping account of the gold, silver, and bronze used in its making.
LifeLesson: Faithful stewardship of holy things is holy work itself.

Name: Izhar
Summary: Izhar was a son of Kohath and a grandson of Levi, and the father of Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
KeyStory: Izhar's son Korah would later lead a rebellion against Moses and Aaron — a warning from within Levi's own house.
RelatedPeople: Kohath; Korah, Son of Izhar; Nepheg; Zichri
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Jethro
Role: Priest of Midian; Father-in-Law of Moses
Summary: Jethro was the priest of Midian, the father of Zipporah, and Moses' father-in-law. He is also called Reuel.
KeyStory: Jethro sheltered Moses in Midian, gave him Zipporah as wife, and later advised him to share the burden of judging Israel — counsel Moses followed.
RelatedPeople: Moses; Zipporah; Gershom; Eliezer, Son of Moses
LifeLesson: Wise counsel from outside the family can be God's gift: Jethro taught Moses to share the load.

Name: Jochebed
Role: Mother of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
Summary: Jochebed was a daughter of Levi, the wife of Amram, and the mother of Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.
KeyStory: When Pharaoh ordered Hebrew boys drowned, Jochebed hid baby Moses three months, then set him in a basket among the reeds — and later nursed him in Pharaoh's own house.
RelatedPeople: Amram; Moses; Aaron; Miriam; Pharaoh's Daughter
LifeLesson: A mother's courage can carry a child from a basket of reeds to the palace — and to a calling.

Name: Korah, Son of Izhar
Summary: Korah was a son of Izhar, a Levite, and the father of Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph — a different Korah from Esau's son.
KeyStory: Korah is named in Exodus among Levi's house; his later rebellion against Moses is told in Numbers, where the earth swallowed him and his followers.
RelatedPeople: Izhar; Assir, Son of Korah; Elkanah, Son of Korah; Abiasaph, Son of Korah; Moses; Aaron
LifeLesson: Gifts and position do not equal God's calling: Korah wanted Aaron's place and lost everything.

Name: Libni
Summary: Libni was a son of Gershon and a grandson of Levi, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Libni is named with his brother Shimi among Gershon's sons in the record of Levi's house.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Mahali
Summary: Mahali was a son of Merari and a grandson of Levi, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Mahali is named with his brother Mushi among Merari's sons in the record of Levi's house.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Mishael
Summary: Mishael was a son of Uzziel and a grandson of Kohath, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Mishael and his brother Elzaphan were called by Moses to carry the bodies of Nadab and Abihu out of the camp.
LifeLesson: Obedience sometimes means hard, holy work no one else wants to do.

Name: Mushi
Summary: Mushi was a son of Merari and a grandson of Levi, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Mushi is named with his brother Mahali among Merari's sons in the record of Levi's house.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Naashon
Summary: Naashon was the son of Amminadab and the brother of Elisheba, and the prince of the tribe of Judah. In Numbers his name is spelled Nahshon.
KeyStory: Naashon led Judah's offerings for the tabernacle and marched at the head of Israel's tribes through the wilderness.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Nadab
Summary: Nadab was the firstborn son of Aaron and Elisheba, and one of the priests of Israel.
KeyStory: Nadab went up Mount Sinai with Moses and saw God, but later offered strange fire before the LORD and died — a warning about worship on God's terms, not ours.
LifeLesson: Closeness to God is no substitute for obedience: Nadab saw God and still offered strange fire.

Name: Nepheg
Summary: Nepheg was a son of Izhar and a grandson of Kohath, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Nepheg is named with his brothers Korah and Zichri among Izhar's sons.
RelatedPeople: Izhar; Korah, Son of Izhar; Zichri
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Nun, Father of Joshua
Summary: Nun was of the tribe of Ephraim, and the father of Joshua, Moses' successor.
KeyStory: Nun is named only as Joshua's father — yet his son led Israel into the land Moses could only see.
LifeLesson: A parent's legacy can be a child who finishes what you only began.

Name: Pharaoh's Daughter
Summary: Pharaoh's daughter found the baby Moses in a basket among the reeds and raised him as her own son in Pharaoh's house.
KeyStory: Though her father had ordered Hebrew boys drowned, she had compassion on the crying child, hired his own mother as his nurse, and named him Moses.
LifeLesson: Compassion can defy even a king's decree — and change the course of a nation.

Name: Phinehas
Summary: Phinehas was the son of Eleazar and the grandson of Aaron, and a priest known for his zeal for God's honor.
KeyStory: Phinehas turned away God's wrath in the wilderness by acting against open sin, and God gave him a covenant of an everlasting priesthood.
LifeLesson: Zeal for God's honor, rightly aimed, can turn away wrath and save a people.

Name: Puah
Summary: Puah was one of the two Hebrew midwives who feared God and refused Pharaoh's order to kill newborn Hebrew boys.
KeyStory: When Pharaoh commanded the midwives to kill every Hebrew son at birth, Puah and Shiphrah let the boys live — and God gave them families of their own.
LifeLesson: Fearing God matters more than fearing a king — even when disobedience is dangerous.

Name: Putiel
Summary: Putiel was the father of the wife of Eleazar, and the grandfather of Phinehas.
KeyStory: Putiel is named only in the genealogy of Aaron's house, as the father of Eleazar's wife.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Shimi
Summary: Shimi was a son of Gershon and a grandson of Levi, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Shimi is named with his brother Libni among Gershon's sons in the record of Levi's house.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Shiphrah
Summary: Shiphrah was one of the two Hebrew midwives who feared God and refused Pharaoh's order to kill newborn Hebrew boys.
KeyStory: When Pharaoh commanded the midwives to kill every Hebrew son at birth, Shiphrah and Puah let the boys live — and God dealt well with them.
LifeLesson: Fearing God matters more than fearing a king — even when disobedience is dangerous.

Name: Uri
Summary: Uri was the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and the father of Bezaleel, the craftsman of the tabernacle.
KeyStory: Uri is named only as Bezaleel's father, in the line that gave Israel its master craftsman.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Uzziel
Summary: Uzziel was a son of Kohath and a grandson of Levi, and the father of Mishael, Elzaphan, and Zithri.
KeyStory: Uzziel's sons Mishael and Elzaphan were the ones called to carry Nadab and Abihu out of the sanctuary after their deaths.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Zichri
Summary: Zichri was a son of Izhar and a grandson of Kohath, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Zichri is named with his brothers Korah and Nepheg among Izhar's sons.
RelatedPeople: Izhar; Korah, Son of Izhar; Nepheg
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Zipporah
Summary: Zipporah was a daughter of Jethro, priest of Midian, and the wife of Moses. She bore him Gershom and Eliezer.
KeyStory: Zipporah married Moses during his years in Midian, and on the journey back to Egypt she acted swiftly to spare Moses' life.
RelatedPeople: Moses; Jethro; Gershom; Eliezer, Son of Moses
LifeLesson: A spouse's quick, brave action can save the very mission God gave.

Name: Zithri
Summary: Zithri was a son of Uzziel and a grandson of Kohath, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Zithri is named with his brothers Mishael and Elzaphan among Uzziel's sons.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Dibri
Summary: Dibri was of the tribe of Dan, and the father of Shelomith.
KeyStory: Dibri is named only as Shelomith's father, in the account of his grandson's blasphemy and stoning.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Shelomith
Summary: Shelomith was the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan, and the mother of the man who blasphemed the Name and was stoned.
KeyStory: Shelomith's son fought with an Israelite in the camp, blasphemed the Name, and was put in custody until Moses inquired of the LORD — and her name is preserved in the law that followed.
LifeLesson: A mother's name can be remembered even in her family's hardest chapter — God does not look away.

Name: Son of Shelomith
Summary: The son of Shelomith — Scripture gives him no name — was a man of mixed parentage, his father an Egyptian, who blasphemed the Name during a fight in the camp.
KeyStory: After he cursed the Name, Moses put him in custody, inquired of the LORD, and the whole congregation stoned him outside the camp — establishing the law that whoever blasphemes the Name shall be put to death.
LifeLesson: Words against God's holy Name are no small thing: what we say about Him reveals what we believe about Him.

Name: Abidan, Son of Gideoni

Name: Balak

LifeLesson: Not all service is seen — some of it is carrying the very walls of worship.
